title: Salsa Announces New Beargrease Carbon and Aluminum Fatbikes
content:
Salsa Cycles has launched an all-new Beargrease fat-tire bike. The latest iteration of the platform is designed for stability and versatility to take on all terrain and conditions.

Salsa’s latest Beargrease is available with both carbon fiber and 6061-T6 aluminum frame options with new Bearpaw carbon and aluminum forks. Its​ geometry aligns more with modern trail bikes than the previous generation.

What’s new about it?

  • Modern trail geometry (longer wheelbase, slacker head tube angle, and steeper seat tube angle) for a more centered position with a modern MTB feel
  • Designed around 27.5 x 4.5″ tires for more float and traction
  • Carbon fiber and 6061-T6 aluminum frame options with new Bearpaw carbon and aluminum forks
  • Three bottle mounts on sizes SM–XL and direct-mount frame bag mounts
  • SRAM UDH compatibility
  • Models & MSRP:
    • Beargrease AL Eagle 70: $1,999 USD, $2,599 CAD
    • Beargrease C Eagle 70: $3,299 USD, $3,999 CAD
    • Beargease C Eagle 90: $4,299 USD, $6,099 CAD
    • Beargrease C GX AXS: $5,999 USD, $8,499 CAD
    • Beargease C Frameset: $1,999 USD, $2,899 CAD

Salsa Cycles launched their first fat-tire bike, Mukluk, back in 2010 and developed the industry’s first carbon fiber fat-tire bike, Beargrease, in 2014. The brand has continued to refine its fat-tire offerings since.

Beargrease is available now at Salsa retailers, with framesets also available on SalsaCycles.com.
